headline: Microsoft adds a risk score for AI agents
dek: The controls limit what an agent can do inside a company as its risk rises, Microsoft says.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The agent already inside
body: Microsoft released security controls for AI agents working inside companies (Microsoft, SiliconANGLE).
According to the company, these agents have too much access to data and systems and can act in ways no one intended.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the score works
s3.body: According to SiliconANGLE, each agent carries a risk score:

points.t: Dynamic Agent Risk rises when the agent strays.
A high score removes write access and leaves read-only.
At the top of the scale, the agent is isolated or halted.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Who Microsoft watches
body: According to SiliconANGLE, the tools now identify 60 kinds of local agents, 35 more than before.
The list includes Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot, according to SiliconANGLE.

stat.cap: kinds of agents detected, SiliconANGLE says

items.t: The company did not share pricing for the new controls.
It did not say when general availability arrives.
It promises more at Microsoft Ignite, SiliconANGLE says.

caption.hook: Microsoft built a real-time risk score to monitor AI agents inside companies.
body: According to Microsoft and SiliconANGLE, each agent gets an identity and a risk score that rises when it strays from what was intended. A high score can remove write access, require human approval or isolate the agent entirely.

SiliconANGLE says Microsoft's tools now detect 60 kinds of local agents, including Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot. The company did not share pricing or a general availability date and promises more details at Microsoft Ignite.
caption.cta: Would your company let an AI agent act without a guardian watching it?
